Hi Jordan / Sam —

Thanks — great questions. I’ve answered each item below with the recommended contractual language where applicable. TL;DR: Redwood supports customer-level region pinning and can ensure inference and persistent logs remain in the pinned region under normal operation. Cross-region failover is configurable (by default restricted to approved backup regions) and we offer customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. See notes below and attached one-pager for a diagram.

1) Encryption
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ by default for all API traffic.
- At rest: All persistent storage (models, snapshots, logs) is encrypted at rest. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we can enable CMK on request (contract-level).
- Recommended contract line: "All customer data at rest and in transit shall be encrypted; customer may elect to use a customer-managed key for encryption of persistent artifacts."

2) Region guarantees / failover behavior
- Region pinning: We offer per-customer region pinning. When you pin to us-west2, inference requests are routed to compute in us-west2 and primary persistent logs are written to storage in us-west2.
- Failover: Automatic failover is optional and can be scoped to a whitelist of backup regions (e.g., us-east1 only). When configured, failover will only route to the approved backup region(s).
- Data movement during failover: In failover mode we do forward the request payload to the backup region to execute inference; however, we can configure transient-only processing (no persistent logs retained in backup) and we can redact or mask PII prior to any cross-region processing if requested.
- Recommended contract line: "Automatic cross-region failover will only occur to customer-approved standby regions; Redwood will not persist PII-containing logs in a standby region unless cross-region replication is expressly enabled by the customer."

3) Backups and replication
- Backups (model checkpoints, KV snapshots) are stored in the customer's primary region by default. Cross-region replication is not enabled by default for Hosted; it can be enabled as an option and will respect CMK settings.
- For Dedicated deployments, customers can choose to enable cross-region snapshots which will be encrypted with the customer KMS.

4) Retention & purge
- Default retention: request logs 90 days, debug traces 30 days, structured outputs (if stored) 90 days.
- Customization: Retention windows are configurable per-account and per-route; we can meet 180-day retention or other regulator-mandated retention requirements via config.
- On-demand purge (DSR): We provide an API and managed ops workflow to purge logs and stored outputs for specific tenant IDs/requests. Purge requests are auditable and we provide confirmation once deletion is completed.

5) Auditability
- We provide immutable audit logs with timestamps, actor identity (API key or user id), action, and resource identifiers. Exports can be delivered to a customer-owned storage bucket on a schedule (daily/weekly) or via API pull.

6) SLA & Dedicated differences
- Hosted (default): data residency is implemented through regional routing and region-specific storage. Cross-region replication is opt-in. KMS CMK support available with contract.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): you get dedicated GPU pools in the chosen region, storage isolated to that region (and stronger contractual guarantees around placement), and easier enablement of CMK + cross-region snapshot options. Pricing for Dedicated is commit-based — I can share a ballpark range after a few details (expected QPS, model family, desired headroom).

Attachments: I've re-attached the region-pinning one-pager and a short checklist for SOC2 evidence. If helpful, I can create a redlined paragraph you can paste into a security questionnaire.

Next steps:
- If you’re comfortable, I suggest a 30-minute technical call with me + our Solutions Engineer (I can set this up) to walk through a simple diagram of failover and purge flows and to get any procurement-specific language for the contract.
- I’ll also prepare a ballpark Dedicated pricing sheet once you confirm expected steady-state QPS and model families (Llama-variant vs other).
